{{Start date and age|2017}}, as ''Como 1907'' | stadium = [[Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia]] | capacity = 13,602 | owner = [[Djarum|Djarum Group]] | chairman = Mirwan Suwarso | chrtitle = President | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Cesc Fàbregas]] | league = {{Italian football updater|Como}} | season = {{Italian football updater|Como2}} | position = {{Italian football updater|Como3}} | website = {{Official URL}} | pattern_la1 = _como2627h | pattern_b1 = _como2627h | pattern_ra1 = _como2627h | pattern_sh1 = _como2627h | pattern_so1 = _socks | leftarm1 = 215AAE | body1 = 215AAE | rightarm1 = 215AAE | shorts1 = FFFFFF | socks1 = 215AAE | pattern_la2 = _como2627a | pattern_b2 = _como2627a | pattern_ra2 = _como2627a | pattern_sh2 = _como2627a | pattern_so2 = _3_stripes_navy | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = | current = 2026–27 Como 1907 season }} '''Como 1907''' ({{IPA|it|ˈkɔːmo}}) is an Italian professional [[football club]] based in [[Como]], [[Lombardy]], that competes in [[Serie A]], the top flight of the [[Italian football league system|Italian football system]]. Founded in 1907 as Como Foot-Ball Club, the team traditionally plays in [[royal blue]] and has hosted home matches at the [[Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia]] since 1928.{{cite web |author=Federazione Italiana Giuoco Calcio |date=2 October 2020 |title=Elenco delle società C.R. Lombardia |url=https://www.crlombardia.it/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/ANNUARIO-SOCIETA-2020-2021.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210618054600/https://www.crlombardia.it/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/ANNUARIO-SOCIETA-2020-2021.pdf |archive-date=18 June 2021 |access-date=11 October 2020}} The club was acquired in 2019 by the Hartono brothers ([[Robert Budi Hartono]] and [[Michael Bambang Hartono]]) through [[Djarum|Djarum Group]].{{Cite web |date=2024-04-03 |title=Como paperone coi fratelli Hartono, Commisso (Fiorentina) e Friedkin (Roma) al top in Serie A: le proprietà più ricche |url=https://www.eurosport.it/geoblocking.shtml |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=Eurosport.it |language=it}} Minority shareholders in the club include head coach [[Cesc Fàbregas]] and former international footballer [[Thierry Henry]].{{Cite web |last=Sportelli |first=Matteo |date=2024-05-24 |title=Renzo Rosso, Giovanni Arvedi e Rocco Commisso: chi sono i proprietari più ricchi del calcio italiano |url=https://forbes.it/2024/05/24/chi-sono-proprietari-ricchi-calcio-italiano/ |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=Forbes Italia |language=it}}{{Cite web |last=Morra |first=Alessio |date=2024-05-10 |title=Come ha fatto il Como a tornare in Serie A: Fabregas, Henry e i proprietari più ricchi in Italia |url=https://www.fanpage.it/sport/calcio/come-ha-fatto-il-como-a-tornare-in-serie-a-fabregas-henry-e-i-proprietari-piu-ricchi-in-italia/ |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=Sport Fanpage |language=it}} Como made its top-tier debut in the [[1913–14 Prima Categoria]] and remained in the top division until its relegation in 1922. During the [[1930–31 Prima Divisione]] season, head coach Gedeon Eugen Lukács guided the team to promotion to [[Serie B]]; Como went undefeated throughout both the regular season and the promotion play-offs, scoring 90 goals and conceding 24 in 32 matches. In the 2000s, severe financial distress led to consecutive relegations for the club. Como was declared bankrupt in 2004 and excluded from professional league participation. Re-established in [[Serie D]]—the top level of non-professional Italian football—the club spent three seasons in the division before earning promotion to Serie C2 in 2007.{{cite web |url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/Notizie/Calcio/27884/Cosenza+e+Como%2C+promozione+in+C2 |publisher=Corriere dello Sport |language=it |access-date=27 April 2008 |date=27 April 2008 |title=Cosenza e Como, promozione in C2 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Following another bankruptcy in 2016, a new corporate entity refounded the club in 2017, re-entering competition in Serie D.{{cite web |title=Stagione Sportiva 2017/2018 Comunicato Ufficiale N°14 del 14/8/2017 |trans-title=Sporting season 2017/2018 Official Statement N°14 of 14/8/2017 |url=http://seried.lnd.it/download/serieD/comunicati/2017-18/cu_014.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825184401/http://seried.lnd.it/download/serieD/comunicati/2017-18/cu_014.pdf |archive-date=25 August 2017 |access-date=25 August 2017 |publisher=[[Italian Football Federation|Federazione Italiana Giuoco Calcio]]|via=[[Lega Nazionale Dilettanti]] |language=it}} Under the ownership of the Hartono brothers—ranked among the world's wealthiest individuals by ''[[Forbes]]'' and the richest owners in Italian football{{Cite web |date=2022-04-06 |title=I 10 proprietari più ricchi del calcio italiano |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/calcio-proprieta-piu-ricche-italia-classifica |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=Sky Sport Italia |language=it}}{{Cite web |date=2024-04-04 |title=Calcio, i proprietari di club più ricchi al mondo |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/calcio-proprietari-piu-ricchi-classifica-forbes |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=Sky Sport Italia |language=it}}—the club climbed back to Serie B before securing promotion to Serie A in 2024, ending a 21-year absence from the top flight.{{Cite web |last=Torrisi |first=Antonio |date=2024-05-10 |title=Il Como è in Serie A: dalla D alla gloria in cinque anni, la visione di SENT è compiuta |url=https://www.goal.com/it/liste/como-in-serie-a-da-quanto-tempo-non-succedeva-chi-e-wise-fabregas-henry-storia/blt2d7f338e04bee2cb |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=Goal.com Italia |language=it}}{{Cite web |last=Donato |first=Lelio |date=2024-07-07 |title=L'ambizioso progetto del Como in Serie A: da Pau Lopez a Varane e Belotti, tutti gli obiettivi |url=https://www.goal.com/it/liste/l-ambizioso-progetto-del-como-in-serie-a-da-pau-lopez-a-varane-e-belotti-tutti-gli-obiettivi/bltdc287c603b003c55 |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=Goal.com Italia |language=it}} Como finished 10th in their [[2024–25 Serie A|return season]]. In the [[2025–26 Serie A|2025–26 season]], the club placed 4th, securing qualification for European competition for the first time since participating in the 1980–81 [[Mitropa Cup]] and earning its debut appearance in the [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].{{cite web |url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/il-como-fa-la-storia-europa-matematica-per-il-2026-27-la-classifica-di-serie-a-aggiornata-2232585 |title=Il Como fa la storia: Europa matematica per il 2026/27. La classifica di Serie A aggiornata |date=10 May 2026 |website=tuttomercatoweb.it |language=Italian |trans-title=Como made history: mathematically [[qualified]] in Europe for 2026/26 [...] }}{{cite web |url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/la-champions-e-storia-ma-non-e-una-favola-nessuno-ha-speso-quanto-il-como-dal-2023-a-oggi-2237802 |title=La Champions è storia, ma non è una favola: nessuno ha speso quanto il Como dal 2023 a oggi |date=24 May 2026 |website=tuttomercatoweb.it |language=Italian}}"}}
